operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Sec. 9. The Secretary of the Treasury, in consultation with the Secretary 
of State, is authorized to take such actions, including the promulgation 
of rules and regulations, and to employ all powers granted to the President 
by IEEPA as may be necessary to carry out the purposes of this order.

any of these functions within the Department of the Treasury. All executive 
departments and agencies of the United States shall take all appropriate 
measures within their authority to implement this order.

7605 Federal Register / Vol. 89, No. 24 / Monday, February 5, 2024 / Presidential Documents 
Executive Order 14115 of February 1, 2024 
Imposing Certain Sanctions on Persons Undermining Peace, 
Security, and Stability in the West Bank 
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, including the International Emergency 
Economic Powers Act (50 U.S.C. 1701 et seq.) (IEEPA), the National Emer-
gencies Act (50 U.S.C. 1601 et seq.) (NEA), section 212(f) and section 215(a) 
of the Immigration and Nationality Act of 1952 (8 U.S.C. 1182(f) and 8 
U.S.C. 1185(a)), and section 301 of title 3, United States Code, 
I, JOSEPH R. BIDEN JR., President of the United States of America, find 
that the situation in the West Bank—in particular high levels of extremist 
settler violence, forced displacement of people and villages, and property 
destruction—has reached intolerable levels and constitutes a serious threat 
to the peace, security, and stability of the West Bank and Gaza, Israel, 
and the broader Middle East region. These actions undermine the foreign 
policy objectives of the United States, including the viability of a two- 
state solution and ensuring Israelis and Palestinians can attain equal measures 
of security, prosperity, and freedom. They also undermine the security of 
Israel and have the potential to lead to broader regional destabilization 
across the Middle East, threatening United States personnel and interests. 
For these reasons, these actions constitute an unusual and extraordinary 
threat to the national security and foreign policy of the United States. 
I hereby declare a national emergency to deal with that threat. 
Accordingly, I hereby order: 
Section 1. All property and interests in property that are in the United 
States, that hereafter come within the United States, or that are or hereafter 
come within the possession or control of any United States person, including 
any foreign branch, of the following persons are blocked and may not 
be transferred, paid, exported, withdrawn, or otherwise dealt in: 
(a) any foreign person determined by the Secretary of State, in consultation 
with the Secretary of the Treasury, or the Secretary of the Treasury, in 
consultation with the Secretary of State: 
(i) to be responsible for or complicit in, or to have directly or indirectly 
engaged or attempted to engage in, any of the following: 
(A) actions—including directing, enacting, implementing, enforcing, or 
failing to enforce policies—that threaten the peace, security, or stability 
of the West Bank; or 
(B) planning, ordering, otherwise directing, or participating in any of 
the following actions affecting the West Bank: 
(1) an act of violence or threat of violence targeting civilians; 
(2) efforts to place civilians in reasonable fear of violence with the 
purpose or effect of necessitating a change of residence to avoid such 
violence; 
(3) property destruction; or 
(4) seizure or dispossession of property by private actors; 
(ii) to be or have been a leader or official of: 
(A) an entity, including any government entity, that has engaged in, 
or whose members have engaged in, any of the activities described in 
subsections (a) or (b) of this section related to the leader’s or official’s 
tenure; or

7606 Federal Register / Vol. 89, No. 24 / Monday, February 5, 2024 / Presidential Documents 
(B) an entity whose property and interests in property are blocked 
pursuant to this order as a result of activities relating to the leader’s 
or official’s tenure; 
(iii) to have materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, 
or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, 
any person blocked pursuant to this order; or 
(iv) to be owned or controlled by, or to have acted or purported to 
act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, any person blocked pursuant 
to this order; or 
(b) any foreign person determined by the Secretary of State, in consultation 
with the Secretary of the Treasury: 
(i) to have committed or have attempted to commit, to pose a significant 
risk of committing, or to have participated in training to commit acts 
of terrorism affecting the West Bank; or 
(ii) to be a leader or official of an entity sanctioned pursuant to subsection 
(b)(i) of this section. 
Sec. 2. The prohibitions in section 1 of this order apply except to the

research_rationale: EO 14115 (signed 2024-02-01, 89 FR 7605-7608), read in full from the held official FR text, finds a threat to the peace, security and stability of the West Bank and declares a national emergency, blocks the property of persons determined under sec. 1 (secs. 1-3), suspends their entry (sec. 4), prohibits evasion and conspiracy (sec. 5), makes IEEPA determinations on donations and notice (secs. 6 and 8), defines terms (sec. 7), authorizes Treasury rules and redelegation (sec. 9), excepts official business (sec. 10), provides for reports to the Congress (sec. 11) and has general provisions (sec. 12). The order has no term, sunset or termination clause: its only dossier own-term leads are the 'consistent with applicable law' condition and the sec. 4(d) comparison to Proclamation 8693, neither an end. EO 14148 sec. 2(hhh) revokes the whole order with no effective-date wording, so effective on signing 2025-01-20. The dossier has no missing line, conflict or current-law lead for this order. The dossier inventory (43 clauses) began after the findings paragraph and split sec. 1(b)(ii) in the middle of a sentence, so the inventory was corrected by override: the preamble findings are added as one clause, and the two fragments of sec. 1(b)(ii) are merged, and the two short items of sec. 1(a)(i)(B), (3) and (4), are merged (too short for the claim-checker to verify) (42 clauses in all). The national-emergency question is stated in the lead clause and in savings_residuals. No amendment, extension, partial revocation or supersession of EO 14115 appears in any held text or OFR edge before 2025-01-20. The Code note at 50 U.S.C. 1701 note ('West Bank') states 'Ex. Ord. No. 14115, Feb. 1, 2024, 89 F.R. 7605, revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 14148, sec. 2(hhh), Jan. 20, 2025, 90 F.R. 8240', consistent with this ending (a machine-extracted lead, not relied on).

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record LSP-EO_14148 (official FR text 90 FR 8237, read once in full, text_sha256 65bf2d86... verified on disk): sec. 2 revokes 78 listed executive actions with no effective-date, delayed-effect or phase-in wording, so each revocation took effect on signing, 2025-01-20; sec. 3(b) directs the DPC and NEC Directors to review and rescind, replace or amend agency actions taken under the listed orders (it preserves no provision, office or right of any listed order); sec. 4(a) is a no-impair clause for statutory authority and OMB functions only; there is no successor delegation, no transfer of functions, funds or property, no pending-matter clause and no exception for any listed order. Own-residual check, reading EO 14115 in full (preamble and secs. 1-12): the order declared a national emergency under IEEPA and the NEA, blocked all property and interests in property of persons determined under sec. 1 and suspended their entry (sec. 4), and sec. 9 authorized the Treasury Secretary to issue rules and to redelegate functions within Treasury. Effects of the order that attached before 2025-01-20 are not undone by its revocation: property blocked and transactions prohibited or evaded under secs. 1-5 before that date, and any liability for violations before it, are accrued matters of an IEEPA instrument, and EO 14148 sec. 2(hhh) revokes the order with no savings clause and no statement of what happens to them (accrued). The sec. 9 redelegation authority and any Treasury listings made under it are exercises of functions the order conferred; they end with the order and no redelegation or regulation under it appears in the eCFR machine search. The national emergency declared in the preamble is not terminated by EO 14148 in so many words; if it was not continued by a notice published within 90 days before 2025-02-01 it lapsed under 50 U.S.C. 1622(d) after the first end, and I found no such notice in any held source, so the claim relies on the revocation of the order as the first end and asserts nothing about the emergency after it. Prefill was 'review' (S1_transfer_wording): decided from the reading and the order as transferred_or_accrued. Bounded search: every held official FR text (EO 1 through EO 14435) was searched for the number 14115 and the title; only EO 14148 sec. 2(hhh) names it as a target (the EO 9372 and 9386 hits are page-index numbers); OFR edges list only EO 14148 and the Proclamation 8693 cross-reference; the three machine searches were read.

Executive Order 14148 of January 20, 2025 
Initial Rescissions of Harmful Executive Orders and Actions 
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, it is hereby ordered as follows: 
Section 1. Purpose and Policy. The previous administration has embedded 
deeply unpopular, inflationary, illegal, and radical practices within every 
agency and office of the Federal Government. The injection of ‘‘diversity, 
equity, and inclusion’’ (DEI) into our institutions has corrupted them by 
replacing hard work, merit, and equality with a divisive and dangerous 
preferential hierarchy. Orders to open the borders have endangered the 
American people and dissolved Federal, State, and local resources that should 
be used to benefit the American people. Climate extremism has exploded 
inflation and overburdened businesses with regulation. 
To commence the policies that will make our Nation united, fair, safe, 
and prosperous again, it is the policy of the United States to restore common 
sense to the Federal Government and unleash the potential of the American 
citizen. The revocations within this order will be the first of many steps 
the United States Federal Government will take to repair our institutions 
and our economy.
